region.name: Investing GA Launch Readiness
region.summary: Planning and status for taking the Investing product from its 5% beta to general availability, including the go/no-go gates, reconciliation and Android parity blockers, the rollout ramp, the experiment freeze, disclosures, pricing sign-off, and team capacity alongside competing Q4 priorities like card issuing.

brief.text:
This region covers the Stencil team's effort to take its Investing product, fractional ETF investing defined in Investing PRD v3 (locked Jul 15), from a 5% beta to general availability. Under the PRD, KYC-verified users buy and sell curated ETFs from their Stencil balance, with DriveWealth as the brokerage partner and business rules living in the `brokerd` service. The GA date has slipped. Q4 planning first set Investing GA as the top priority with an Oct 6 target, ahead of the Series B close, SOC 2 gaps, post-close hiring (a draft plan of about a dozen engineering hires over 9 months) and card issuing. The launch checklist now targets Oct 20, and that date is at risk. Go/no-go #2 is set for Oct 16. Renee Alvarez owns the regulatory and compliance section of the checklist. Compliance, bank, ops, support and marketing items are cleared or ready. Support macros, the DriveWealth escalation path, the 5% beta and the metrics dashboard are done. Still open are a corrected-positions support macro, go/no-go #2 itself, the GA ramp plan and the held GA announcement.

Two recorded decisions define the gates. GA requires two consecutive days of fully reconciled positions, and Android parity is a GA blocker. The reconciliation fix is the main risk. After it lands, a one-time notice and email go to 46 users with corrected positions. Open risks flag that a late fix merge could leave only one clean reconciliation day before go/no-go #2, and that a review slip would push GA past Oct 20 (owner Devon). For Android parity, the funding screen needs three things to match iOS: a display of remaining daily capacity under the $2,500 per-user-per-day funding cap, an auto-invest cadence picker, and a disclosure sheet. Because the rules live in `brokerd`, this is UI-only work, tracked in an owner/status table as of Oct 8, and Android performance remains a concern. The proposed GA ramp is 25%, then 50%, then 100%, with each step gated on clean reconciliation. An open question is how ramp timing lines up with the board meeting. The support ticket rate is still above target. The disclosures item B2 was closed at standup, but an open todo still has Renee Alvarez delivering final disclosures copy (severity 28). Hana Ito is the single reviewer for investing disclosures, which is a bottleneck.

Adjacent topics include pricing, the experiment freeze and capacity. The board was asked to sign off on a $9.99 price, with a pricing revisit allowed 90 days post-launch, for its July 28 meeting. Whether beta users pay was left open, and the conversion model, trial-expiry UX and board pre-read each had owners. A growth experiment freeze protects onboarding and money movement. An Oct 6 exception approved a referral test and a weekly digest push starting Oct 12, since neither touches those flows, with action items assigned to Kavi and Renee. Still open is whether onboarding experiments restart at GA or at GA+14 days, with concerns about morale and contaminated results. On capacity, Marcus Bell is at capacity, Nadia Okafor is on a manager-track trial, and a senior iOS candidate is asking above band (risk severity 27, owner Nadia), with comp band timing unresolved. A Q4 card issuing soft launch could collide with Investing GA and Series B diligence. Typical questions this region answers include what blocks GA, the go/no-go criteria, the ramp plan, the funding cap, disclosures status and owners, and how GA fits against other Q4 priorities.

items.title: Is the investing GA on October 20 at risk? What's blocking it and who owns each blocker?
items.body:
## Short answer: yes, it's at risk — and the map says so explicitly

"GA target Oct 20, **at risk**" is the standing language across the launch map, the product teamspace, and the Oct 9 status rollup [c13][c10][c3]. The decision isn't made yet: go/no-go #2 on **Friday Oct 16** decides GA for **Tuesday Oct 20**, yes or no [c9][c30]. Go/no-go #1 on Sep 29 was a NO-GO [c13][c12].

## The blockers and their owners

Three blockers came out of go/no-go #1. One is closed, two are open [c15][c30]:

| # | Blocker | Owner | Status (as of Oct 9) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Position reconciliation fix | **Devon Park** | In code review; rollout plan being written | Oct 14 |
| B2 | Disclosures final review | **Hana Ito** | Signed Oct 7 — **cleared** | Done |
| B3 | Android parity (2 screens) | **Nadia Okafor** | Order confirmation done; performance detail in progress | Oct 15 |

**B1 — reconciliation (Devon Park).** This is the hard gate. 0.4% of investing positions are off by fractional shares against DriveWealth, all tracing to corporate-action events — a stock split in an underlying ETF holding. Stencil's position ledger applies the split ratio and rounds; DriveWealth carries more precision [c16]. The note is blunt: positions that don't reconcile to the broker block GA outright, and "everything else is negotiable" [c13]. The PR is in review and verified against all 46 affected positions, but still needs a re-run with 0 mismatches [c7][c8].

**B3 — Android parity (Nadia Okafor).** Two screens, merged behind a feature flag. The funding screen needs three things to match iOS: remaining daily capacity under the $2,500/user/day cap, an auto-invest cadence picker, and a disclosure sheet. Because the business rules live in `brokerd`, this is UI-only work. Open items are the flag-gated merge, design QA (paired with Lin, who did iOS), disclosure verification, and Play Store submission. Android performance remains a concern [c28][c29].

## The specific thing most likely to break the date

The GO criteria require **100% of positions reconciled on two consecutive daily runs after the fix** [c30]. If Devon's fix lands Oct 14, the Oct 14 and Oct 15 runs are the bare minimum — there is no slack. The agenda names the risk directly: "The fix lands late on Oct 14 and the Oct 15 run is our only clean day. Then we either accept one day or slip" [c30]. That's also tracked as a standing risk on the region ("only one clean reconciliation day before go/no-go #2"), with the GA-slip risk owned by **Devon** [c29][c11].

Full GO criteria: B1/B2/B3 closed with evidence, two consecutive clean runs, no open SEV1/SEV2 touching money movement, and Hana confirming no compliance objection. Hana holds a **veto on compliance grounds**; Renee chairs, with Renee, Maya Chen and Aleks Varga as decision makers [c30][c9].

## Second-order risk: the board meeting

The board meeting is **Oct 21** — one day after the target GA, and the first attended by Northfield observer Ravi Menon [c1]. A second NO-GO would land in the board pre-read on Oct 16 [c30]. There's an unresolved split on timing even if it's a GO: Kavi wants to ramp to 25% on Oct 20, Maya prefers waiting until after the board [c30]. The ramp plan itself is 25% Oct 20 → 50% Oct 22 → 100% Oct 26, each step gated on clean reconciliation (Kavi owns the plan, due Oct 16) [c30][c29].

A GA slip past Oct 20 is also a named **Series B closing risk** alongside the Sep 26 incident and open SOC 2 gaps, with investing readiness rated a probable diligence question [c2].

## Open prep items before Oct 16

- Devon: land the reconciliation fix by **Oct 14** [c30]
- Nadia: ship Android parity for both screens by **Oct 15** [c30]
- Renee: refresh the launch checklist and send the pre-read by **Oct 15** [c30]
- Kavi: GA ramp plan by **Oct 16** [c30]
- Renee: run go/no-go #2 on **Oct 16** [c30]

Two notes on adjacent signals: a related risk flags "20x DriveWealth load untested" (owner Devon) [c3], and a separate open question asks whether to hold GA for both platforms if Android slips — i.e., iOS-only GA may be a fallback, though no decision is recorded [c29]. One more date-pressure item sits beside this: Maya owns the written Pillar remediation plan due Oct 15, and four deadlines between 10/12 and 10/17 all route through her [c3][c30].
